brief.summary: A widely used consumer site and app for finding and comparing bookable campgrounds and individual campsites across public parks and private campgrounds, used mostly by casual weekend campers.
brief.user: Renee Watanabe, a parent of two kids (6 and 9) planning her family's first camping trip ever. She has a borrowed four-person tent and a minivan, is a little nervous, and is browsing on her phone at lunch with no idea what 'walk-in site' or 'primitive' means.
brief.moment: She wants a campsite for Memorial Day weekend, May 22–25, 2027, within about three hours' drive of Sacramento. Her must-haves are flush toilets and showers, somewhere near a lake or swimming area, shade, and room for the kids to ride bikes; her husband wants to avoid generator noise. brief.data: About 2,300 campgrounds in the region; 338 within a 3-hour drive of Sacramento with at least one site open May 22–25. Each campground has name (e.g., 'Pine Hollow Lakeside – State Park', 'Cedar Flat Family Camp – private'), operator type, drive time, nightly price range ($28–$95), amenities (flush toilets, showers, potable water, playground, lake access, camp store), generator rules and quiet hours, an average rating out of 5 with review count, photos, and the share of sites still available. Individual sites (e.g., 140 at Pine Hollow) have site number, type (tent, RV, walk-in, group), shade level, max occupants and vehicles, distance to the restroom in meters, and per-night availability. Renee has saved 3 campgrounds so far; recent reviews mention 'mosquitoes in late May' and 'loop C is loud'.
